title: Rational root and central directions and a finite-index weight-lattice embedding
statement: Let $M$ be a free abelian group of finite rank, that is, a free $\mathbf Z$-module with a finite basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Spans have the meaning of [def-weil-submodule-span]. Let $R\subset M\setminus\{0\}$ be finite, with a bijection $\alpha\mapsto c_\alpha$ to a subset of $M^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(M,\mathbf Z)$. Assume $c_\alpha(\alpha)=2$, each $s_\alpha(m)=m-c_\alpha(m)\alpha$ permutes $R$, the subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(M)$ generated by the $s_\alpha$ is finite, and $\mathbf Q\alpha\cap R=\{\alpha,-\alpha\}$. Put $E=M\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$, $V=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf Q}R$, and $Z=\{z\in E:c_\alpha(z)=0\text{ for all }\alpha\in R\}$, extending all $c_\alpha$ rationally. Then $E=V\oplus Z$. The restrictions $\bar c_\alpha=c_\alpha|_V$ make $R$ a reduced crystallographic root system in $V$: $R$ spans $V$, $\bar c_\alpha(\alpha)=2$, its reflections permute $R$, $\bar c_\alpha(R)\subset\mathbf Z$, and $\mathbf Q\alpha\cap R=\{\alpha,-\alpha\}$. The coroots span $V^\vee$ and are the unique rational functionals giving the indicated root reflections. The weight lattice $P=\{v\in V:\bar c_\alpha(v)\in\mathbf Z\text{ for all }\alpha\in R\}$ is free of rank $\dim V$ and contains the root lattice $Q_R=\mathbf ZR$ with finite index. If $\pi_V,\pi_Z$ are the two projections, then $C=\pi_Z(M)$ is free of rank $\dim Z$, $\pi_V(M)\subseteq P$, and $j:M\to P\oplus C$, $m\mapsto(\pi_Vm,\pi_Zm)$, is injective with finite cokernel. Moreover $j(\alpha)=(\alpha,0)$ and $c_\alpha(m)=\bar c_\alpha(\pi_Vm)$. The zero lattice and empty root system are included.

source.place: Appendix C.29, C.34--C.35, C.41--C.44, printed pp.614--618; Exercise 21-4, printed p.461 (rational root/central decomposition).

proof.text: Choose a finite $\mathbf Z$-basis $(e_i)$ of $M$. Tensor coordinates identify $E$ with $\mathbf Q^n$: $e_i\otimes q$ maps to the vector with coordinate $q$ at $i$, with inverse $(q_i)\mapsto\sum_i e_i\otimes q_i$. In these coordinates $M\to E$ is the usual injection $\mathbf Z^n\to\mathbf Q^n$. Each $c_\alpha$ extends by $c_\alpha(\sum_iq_ie_i)=\sum_iq_ic_\alpha(e_i)$. The formulas give $s_\alpha^2=1$ and $s_\alpha(\alpha)=-\alpha$. Thus $V$ is stable under every reflection. Finiteness, spanning, nonzero roots, normalization, integrality on roots and reducedness on $V$ are precisely the hypotheses restricted to $V$, proving all the listed root-system axioms.

source.place: C.28--C.29, pp.613--614; explicit basis coordinates and restriction of the reflection formula.

proof.text: Let $W$ be the finite subgroup in the hypothesis, acting rationally on $E$. In the coordinates of step 1 put $B_0(x,y)=\sum_i x_i y_i$ and $B(x,y)=\sum_{w\in W}B_0(wx,wy)$. This is a rational symmetric bilinear form, and $B(x,x)>0$ for $x\ne0$: every summand is nonnegative and the identity summand is positive. For $h\in W$, reindexing $w\mapsto wh$ gives $B(hx,hy)=B(x,y)$. For $\alpha\in R$ use $s_\alpha\alpha=-\alpha$ to compute $$B(x,\alpha)=B(s_\alpha x,s_\alpha\alpha)=-B(x,\alpha)+c_\alpha(x)B(\alpha,\alpha).$$ Hence $c_\alpha(x)=2B(x,\alpha)/B(\alpha,\alpha)$ for every $x\in E$.

source.place: C.19--C.20, p.611 (finite-group averaging and reflection formula), applied to E and its given finite W.

proof.text: The formula in step 2 shows $Z=\{z:B(z,v)=0\text{ for every }v\in V\}$. Choose a rational basis $v_1,\ldots,v_r$ of $V$ from its finite spanning set $R$, successively discarding dependent vectors. The Gram matrix $G=(B(v_i,v_j))$ is invertible over $\mathbf Q$: if $Gt=0$, then $B(\sum t_iv_i,\sum t_iv_i)=0$, so positivity and independence force $t=0$. For each $x\in E$ solve $\sum_i t_i B(v_i,v_j)=B(x,v_j)$, and set $\pi_Vx=\sum_i t_iv_i$, $\pi_Zx=x-\pi_Vx$. These are rational linear maps with images in $V,Z$. If $v\in V\cap Z$, $B(v,v)=0$ forces $v=0$. Thus $E=V\oplus Z$, and these are its projections.

source.place: C.43--C.44, p.618, with the rational orthogonal-projection calculation supplied using C.19--C.20.

proof.text: On $V$, the map $v\mapsto B(-,v)$ to $V^\vee$ has invertible Gram matrix $G$. Step 2 expresses $\bar c_\alpha$ as the nonzero rational multiple $2B(-,\alpha)/B(\alpha,\alpha)$. Since $R$ spans $V$, these coroots therefore span $V^\vee$. If $f:V\to\mathbf Q$ has $f(\alpha)=2$ and $v\mapsto v-f(v)\alpha$ preserves $R$, apply [lem-sfb-finite-spanning-reflection-uniqueness] with $U=V$, $S=R$, $a=\alpha$, and $g=\bar c_\alpha$. Its finite spanning and normalization hypotheses hold by step 1. This gives $f=\bar c_\alpha$, including the usual uniqueness interpretation where preservation of the root set, rather than an already specified map, characterizes the reflection.

The map $t:P\to\mathbf Z^R$, $v\mapsto(\bar c_\alpha(v))_\alpha$, is an injective group homomorphism: its kernel is $V\cap Z=0$. By [lem-weil-subgroup-finite-free-abelian-group-free], its image, and therefore $P$, has a finite $\mathbf Z$-basis $p_1,\ldots,p_s$. Integrality of $c_\alpha(\beta)$ for roots gives $Q_R\subseteq P$. The $p_i$ are rationally independent, since multiplying a rational relation by a common denominator gives an integer relation. They span $V$, because they integrally generate $P$, which contains the spanning set $R$. Thus $s=\dim V$.

source.place: C.26, p.613, and C.35, p.615; the finite-subgroup freeness input is the existing Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: Express the finitely many $p_i$ in the root basis $v_1,\ldots,v_r$ chosen in step 3. Choose a positive integer $D$ divisible by the denominators of all these rational coefficients (take $D=1$ for an empty list). Then $Dp_i\in\sum_j\mathbf Z v_j\subseteq Q_R$, so $DP\subseteq Q_R\subseteq P$. Each class of $P/Q_R$ has a representative $\sum_i a_ip_i$ with $0\leq a_i<D$, by reducing integer basis coefficients modulo $D$. There are at most $D^s$ such representatives; hence $Q_R$ has finite index in $P$.

source.place: C.26, p.613: finiteness of P(R)/Q(R), with denominators and representatives written explicitly.

proof.text: The group $C=\pi_Z(M)$ is generated by the finitely many $\pi_Z(e_i)$, and is torsion-free because it is a subgroup of the rational vector space $Z$. Apply [lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free] to obtain a finite $\mathbf Z$-basis $d_1,\ldots,d_t$ of $C$. It is rationally independent by clearing denominators in any rational relation. It spans $Z$: for $z\in Z$ write $z=\sum_i q_i e_i$ in $E$ and apply $\pi_Z$ to get $z=\sum_i q_i\pi_Z(e_i)$. Therefore $t=\dim Z$. For $m\in M$, step 3 gives $m=\pi_Vm+\pi_Zm$ and $c_\alpha(\pi_Zm)=0$. Thus $\bar c_\alpha(\pi_Vm)=c_\alpha(m)\in\mathbf Z$ and $\pi_V(M)\subseteq P$.

source.place: C.43, p.618, and Exercise 21-4, p.461; C.35, p.615, integrality of the projected root component.

proof.text: The map $j(m)=(\pi_Vm,\pi_Zm)$ is now a well-defined homomorphism $M\to P\oplus C$, and its kernel is zero because summing its coordinates recovers $m\in E$. Under the rational direct-sum identification, a basis of $P\oplus C$ consists of $(p_i,0)$ and $(0,d_j)$, and its rational span is $E$. Express their sums in the original rational basis $(e_i)$, and choose a positive integer $N$ clearing all these coefficients. Then every such basis vector multiplied by $N$ is $j(m)$ for an $m\in M$. Consequently $N(P\oplus C)\subseteq j(M)$. Reducing basis coefficients modulo $N$ gives at most $N^{s+t}$ representatives for $(P\oplus C)/j(M)$; this is the finite cokernel asserted.

source.place: C.43, p.618, finite-index lattice comparison; explicit denominator argument for the direction M into P plus C.

proof.text: For $\alpha\in R\subseteq V$, the projections satisfy $\pi_V\alpha=\alpha$ and $\pi_Z\alpha=0$, so $j(\alpha)=(\alpha,0)$. The identity $c_\alpha(m)=\bar c_\alpha(\pi_Vm)$ was proved in step 7. If $R=\varnothing$, then $V=0$, $Z=E$, $P=0$, $C=M$, and $j(m)=(0,m)$ is an isomorphism. The coroot spanning and uniqueness assertions are vacuous on the zero space. If also $M=0$, all bases, sums and products above are empty and both quotient groups are trivial. Thus no nonempty-root or positive-rank hypothesis has entered the proof.

source.place: C.43, p.618, toral case; explicit rank-zero and empty-root checks.

proof_origin.place: Appendix C.3, C.19--C.20, C.26, C.29, C.35 and C.43--C.44, pp.608--618; Exercise 21-4, p.461. The decomposition uses the finite-group averaging of C.19 on E, with Gram matrices and denominator comparisons expanded explicitly.
